newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Ridley says in north America talks.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Ridley says in north America talks.

text.p: Stockfeed producer Ridley Corp Ltd said on Wednesday it has had discussions for the potential purchase of a stockfeed operation in North America worth about A$100 million, but was still some way off making a decision.
"We have been in discussions with people overseas about feed milling operations," Ridley Corp managing director Gary Busenshut told reporters after the company's annual meeting.
He said that if Ridley Corp was to go ahead with such an acquisition, it could be done by the end of the March quarter of 1997.
Busenshut said the discussions had been with people in North America, but he said he could not narrow it down to the United States or Canada.
Ridley bought Canadian pig-food supplier Feed-rite in 1994 and had since added on several other smaller businesses in Canada and the United States.

Busenshut said that Ridley had looked to spend about A$100 million in its bid for Joe White Maltings Ltd and if, as expected, the bid was not successful then Ridley would look to spend about that much on any North American acquisition.
"That's the sort of bite that would fit well for us," he said.
"If it's something that we want to pursue, it would be by the first quarter of the new year (calendar 1997)," he said.
"We're a long way before we say yes we want this business for this price."
Busenshut repeated his chairman John Keniry's comment that Ridley was still interested in buying a malster in Australia if the Joe White bid fell through.
The A$98 million offer was rejected by Joe White and Ridley has said it would not increase the offer before it closes on November 8. Ridley currently has about 18 percent of Joe White.
Busenshut also said Ridley may be interested in a malster overseas, now that Ridley had built some expertise in the area during its bid for Ridley.
"We've learnt a fair bit about malting offshore and we could consider doing something offshore in malting."
Ridley's shares were down one cent at A$1.68 at 2.20 p.m. (0320 GMT)
